scope: Kayenta Games Obsession second-edition base/core; standard 16-round, 2–4-player multiplayer; original base objectives; marked expansions, optional variants and alternate modes excluded.
assessment: No material rules error or important omission found within the stated base/core scope. Quantities, timing, costs, destinations, exceptions, courtship, scoring and final conditions are consistent with the permitted primary sources. Printed component requirements remain necessary for ordinary tile and guest details, as the summary explicitly states.

sources_reviewed.coverage: Core setup pp.8–12; complete standard play pp.16–24; base detailed rules pp.26–30 and 35–42; relevant FAQ pp.76–79; base family and unique guest entries pp.80–85; all unmarked base improvement entries pp.86–104; VP entries p.105; all entries labelled Base pp.106–111. Expansion/variant text was distinguished from applicable base rules.
Direct PDF inspection, including embedded standard Alderley Hall board illustration on p.12 to independently verify numbered event spaces.
Both pages read directly. Applicable p.2 seasonal-flowchart correction confirmed; expansion/solo errata excluded.
Only pp.7 and 14 read directly, exclusively for unchanged base reputation-objective meaning: maximum level, with Max representing standard level 7. No gameplay or seasonal flow imported.

checked_claims.claim: Standard game consists of four seasons, twelve ordinary turns per player, and four courtship events with no service rotation, monument income, Servants’ Hall use or player turns.
Family selection begins left of random first player; setup reputation, five servants, five starting tiles, family cards, starter guest handling, five objectives and all four base family bonuses.
Servants for Hire quantities; unused supply removed; selected double-sided monuments equal players plus one, at most one Estate monument; activity-to-monument tiles unaffected.
Initial six distinct market tiles obey PR3-or-less, no Servants’ Hall, no double-sided monument; duplicates stack; initial sides and ascending sorting order.
Rotation moves Quarters first and Expended second; each servant advances once; events precede ongoing effects; screening level fixed before choosing activity.
Exact gentry counts/types, gender includes family, casual/prestige excludes family, complete service, mandatory favours, positives before negatives, and drawn invites entering hand.
Cleanup expends all used servants, discards played gentry personally, upgrades/returns activity tile, and only last player advances the round marker.
Pass sequence, all-service and discard recovery, ongoing effects, £200-or-refresh benefit, purchase permission and no base hiring-on-pass.
Village Fair at 3/9, Draw Objectives at 6, Builders’ Holiday at 11, National Holiday at 14 and courtships at 4/8/12/16; event effects and timing.
source_refs: Compendium p.12, standard Alderley Hall board illustration

checked_claims.claim: Reputation increments versus levels; minimum 1.1, standard maximum 7.5; losses, protection, acquisition/scoring independent of PR, fixed screening, National Holiday and family/Fairchild exceptions.
Special actions cost 2/3/4 reputation for £100/one Quarters servant/market refresh; repeatability and refresh limit; excess reputation can be spent during favours.
source_refs: FAQ pp.77–78, Reputation and Special Actions

checked_claims.claim: Money public, supply unlimited, no transfers in this mode, negative money must be paid and can use positive favours, borrowing or VP-card funds.
Base servant substitutions and uniqueness; Butler’s Room hiring/recruiting, no underbutler hiring; Butler’s Pantry only underbutler source, immediate Expended destination and subsequent availability.
source_refs: Compendium p.88, Brushing Room, Butler’s Pantry and Butler’s Room

checked_claims.claim: Servants’ Quarters tile permits use of one servant from Quarters without paying Service Help; no direct Expended-to-Available move from Service Help.
Gentry ownership, no hand limit, family dismissal immunity, optional dismissal from hand/activity/discard to deck bottom, screening reveal rules and casual respectable/unsavoury definitions.
Base family favours/VP, Young Lady conditional male-prestige bonus, both base Fairchild favours/service/VP and base gossip effects; family-only immunity does not extend to guest Fairchilds.
source_refs: Compendium p.83, Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild
Compendium pp.84–85, Florence Oliver and Elizabeth Perkins
Compendium pp.35–36, family and guest dismissal rules

checked_claims.claim: Mandatory normal upgrades, ongoing-only restrictions, hybrid alternating categories, monument timing, suite-to-monument transition, Servants’ Hall and Barn.
source_refs: Compendium p.101, Servants’ Hall and South Lawn

checked_claims.claim: Heritage doubles all favours; Queen’s doubles one chosen favour; Lionheart draws/keeps a prestige guest with no personal service and excludes negative favours from doubling; all suites fixed at one guest.

Private Study one-use activity and upgraded Village Fair benefit; Main Library objective/VP sides; Long Gallery count reduction; base West Terrace remains activity with exact three family and upgraded invite-plus-optional-dismissal.
One normal tile purchase; price modifier and £100 floor; duplicates prohibited; Reserve £300 base, unrestricted inspection/selection, staged Service/PR1 routing and Wine Cellar exception.
source_refs: Compendium pp.20 and 40, buying and Reserve

checked_claims.claim: Refill slides existing tiles, stacks duplicates and sorts new tiles; refresh sets old market aside until replacement completed and does not remove Reserve.
source_refs: Compendium p.41, Refilling & Refreshing the Market

checked_claims.claim: Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase permit multiple fixed-price purchases from one unchanged market, with no intervening refill, slide or refresh.
Base objective draw/discard totals, hidden bottom-deck discards, extra retained objectives and no upgrade requirement for tile objectives.

VP-card benefit-or-points choice, drawing/own-turn/final use windows, bottom-deck disposal and every listed benefit quantity and destination, including full service refresh and one discarded gentry returning to hand.
Courtship return of Fairchilds, theme scoring including negative VP and current hybrids, seasonal ties, objective discard, Reserve-refresh-theme-anticlockwise-first-player sequence.
Final courtship totals four themes with repeated categories repeated; reputation-level tie break, final rewards/discard/action window, and final Fairchild alone retaining its VP.

Final scoring includes tiles, all retained gentry, fulfilled objectives, reputation 1/3/6/10/15/21/28, every servant at 2 VP, £200 units and unused VP cards; correct Fairchild/reputation-level/shared-victory tie breaks.

All thirty base objective entries: ten separate group requirements/values, two guest bonuses, five category bonuses, six servant objectives, four individual tiles and reputation/monument/wealth bonuses; expansion replacements excluded.
The base seven-VP reputation objective requires maximum level (standard level 7), independent of wheel position; supplemental source used solely for that clarification.
source_refs: Official Super Meeple French base rulebook p.14, scoring example for objectives
Official Super Meeple French base rulebook p.7, standard Max equals level 7

checked_claims.claim: Selected current compendium standard flow includes a full market refresh after each of first three courtships; legacy seasonal flowchart omission is corrected, while other corrigendum items concern excluded modes/expansions.
source_refs: Compendium p.23, End of Season and designer note

independence_statement: This was a fresh independent source audit. I read the specified summary snapshot and the permitted authoritative sources, including only the permitted French pages for the unchanged reputation objective. I did not read questions, answer keys, reader responses, grades, prior audits or other QA files; did not communicate with readers; and did not edit or repair the summary. No prior verdict was assumed.
